title: How to start a real estate business
summary: Learn how to start a real estate business. Get practical guidance on licensing, business planning, networking, marketing strategies, and smart financial management for long-term success.
body_text: Real estate is a broad industry that includes residential sales, commercial leasing, property investment, and brokerage services. Each niche has its own challenges and opportunities. Choosing the right area early on helps you build expertise and credibility, allowing you to tailor your offering to a specific real estate niche. Before investing time and money, build knowledge and a strong understanding of how real estate works. Learn the essentials, including property valuation, local market trends, contracts and negotiations, financing options such as mortgages and loans, and the laws and regulations within your area. There are numerous resources available to help you get started, including: Online courses offered through platforms like Udemy or Coursera Educational content from local real estate boards YouTube channels such as BiggerPockets and Graham Stephan. Licensing is a crucial step in launching a real estate business if you intend to buy or sell properties on behalf of others. Most states require completing a state-approved pre-licensing course, passing the real estate exam, and submitting applications and fees to your state board. After obtaining your license, you’ll typically need to work under a brokerage to gain experience and join a local real estate association for networking and credibility. A well-structured business plan is essential for launching and growing a successful real estate business. It should clearly define your mission, brand positioning, and strategies for long-term growth. Start by identifying your target market (whether it's buyers, sellers, or renters) and outlining both short-term goals and long-term objectives, such as expanding into commercial real estate or opening a brokerage. Include detailed revenue projections from commissions, referral fees, or investment returns, and map out your income strategy, marketing plan, and budget. Don't forget to account for startup costs, including licensing fees, marketing and branding expenses, website and CRM tools, as well as office or transportation needs. A comprehensive business plan not only keeps you focused but also positions your real estate business for sustainable success. Register your business Once your business plan is in place, the next step is to make your real estate business official. Start by choosing a business name that reflects your brand and check its availability in your state. Then, register your business structure based on your goals and liability preferences. Pro tip: Open a dedicated business bank account to keep finances organized and consider obtaining insurance, such as errors and omissions coverage, to protect against potential risks. Fuel Growth with Business Premium Savings Put your profits to work with a high-yield business savings account. Accelerate your real estate business growth with a high-yield business savings account. With no monthly maintenance fees and competitive interest rates, Business Premium Savings helps you grow your cash reserves and stay financially strong as you scale. Get Started Learn More Success in real estate depends heavily on relationships. Building a strong network can open doors to new opportunities and help you grow your business faster. Connect with other agents and brokers, mortgage lenders, lawyers, accountants, contractors, inspectors, and property investors. Pro tip : Attend open houses, local networking events, and industry meetups to establish valuable connections. A solid network not only provides referrals but also gives you access to trusted professionals who can support your clients and enhance your credibility. Clients won’t come unless they know you exist, so marketing is one of the most critical aspects of building a successful real estate business. Utilize a combination of strategies to maximize visibility and attract potential leads: Social media: Instagram, TikTok, Facebook for listings and content. Property listing websites for exposure. Traditional methods: cold calling and door-to-door marketing. Email newsletters to stay connected with prospects. Personal website & Google Business profile for credibility and local SEO. Remember, consistency matters more than perfection. Regular, authentic engagement will build trust and attract clients over time. Deliver exceptional service The best marketing strategy in real estate is providing outstanding service. When clients feel valued and supported throughout the buying or selling process, they are far more likely to refer you to others and return for future transactions. Focus on clear communication, transparency, and going the extra mile to meet client needs. Building trust and delivering results will create a strong reputation that drives organic growth and word-of-mouth referrals. This is arguably the most powerful form of marketing in the industry. Build a strong brand A recognizable personal brand sets you apart in a competitive real estate market. Focus on consistent messaging across all platforms, professional branding, and delivering value through educational content and exceptional client experiences. A strong brand builds trust, attracts long-term clients, and positions you as an authority in your niche. Track income and expenses carefully to maintain profitability and avoid cash flow issues. Set aside money for taxes early to prevent surprises, and as your business grows, consider hiring an accountant to ensure compliance and optimize your financial strategy. Opening a dedicated business bank account is crucial for maintaining the separation between personal and business finances. Solutions like Axos Business Banking offer convenient online tools, low fees, and features designed for small businesses and entrepreneurs. Strong financial discipline is key to long-term stability and success. Use your profits strategically to fuel growth. Invest in marketing, technology, and tools that enhance efficiency and enable you to reach a broader range of clients. As your business expands, consider hiring support staff or additional agents to manage increasing demand and maintain high-quality service. Scaling strategically ensures sustainable growth without sacrificing client satisfaction. Starting a real estate business is a journey that requires planning, persistence, and a focus on delivering value. By taking the time to understand the industry, build relationships, and stay consistent with your efforts, you set yourself up for long-term success. Remember, growth doesn’t happen overnight, but with a clear vision and commitment to excellence, you can create a business that thrives and stands out in a competitive market. Stay focused, keep learning, and trust the process. The results will follow.

title: How Preclinical PDX Studies Help Guide PSMA Radioligand Development
summary: This blog highlights key findings, but the full study includes detailed radiochemistry validation, biodistribution data, tumortotissue ratios, and efficacy results across multiple PDX models.
body_text: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, or mCRPC, remains a major clinical challenge. While prostate-specific membrane antigen, PSMA, has emerged as a highly promising therapeutic target, differences in tumor biology, target expression, and radiopharmaceutical behavior continue to influence clinical outcomes. For PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies to reach their full potential, developers need preclinical models that reliably capture both tumor complexity and biodistribution behavior in vivo. At AACR 2026, we presented data showing how patientderived xenograft (PDX) models can be used to evaluate PSMA-targeted radiopharmaceuticals at multiple levels. This included radiochemistry quality, biodistribution, and tumor selectivity. The work focused on two clinically relevant agents, [177Lu]LuPSMA617 and [225Ac]AcPSMA617, tested across a panel of mCRPC PDX models with variable PSMA expression. Why PDX models are critical for radiopharmaceutical development Radiopharmaceutical therapies rely on far more than target binding alone. Successful translation depends on tumor uptake, retention, clearance from healthy tissues, and therapeutic index. Traditional cell line models fail to capture the architectural and microenvironmental features that shape these processes in patients. PDX models preserve the genetic heterogeneity and tissue organization of the original human tumor. This makes them particularly well suited for studying radioligand distribution and efficacy in vivo. In the context of PSMA-targeted therapies, PDX models allow us to directly evaluate how differences in PSMA expression and tumor biology influence radiotracer uptake in clinically relevant tumor models. Designing a clinically relevant PSMA radiopharmaceutical study In this study, we evaluated PSMA617 labeled with either lutetium177 or actinium225 across multiple prostate cancer PDX models representing metastatic, castration-resistant disease. The models spanned a range of PSMA expression levels, enabling us to assess how target expression directly relates to biodistribution. We first confirmed robust radiochemical performance. PSMA617 was efficiently labeled with both isotopes, achieving high radiochemical purity that met stringent quality standards. Establishing radiochemistry consistency is a critical first step before moving into in vivo evaluation, particularly for comparative studies involving different isotopes. How biodistribution studies inform target specificity and safety Following radiotracer administration, we conducted biodistribution analyses at defined time points to quantify uptake across tumors and major organs. Rather than relying on a single model, we assessed multiple PDXs to capture biologically driven variability. Across the panel, tumor uptake correlated strongly with PSMA expression levels. Models with high PSMA expression showed selective and robust radiotracer accumulation, while low-PSMA models demonstrated minimal uptake. This clear relationship confirms biological predictability and reinforces the value of molecularly annotated PDX panels when evaluating PSMA-targeted therapies. Importantly, although both [177Lu]LuPSMA617 and [225Ac]AcPSMA617 demonstrated tumor targeting, differences emerged in tumor-to-normal tissue ratios. These distinctions highlight why side-by-side preclinical evaluation is essential when selecting isotopes and dosing strategies for clinical development. Comparing beta- and alpha-emitting PSMA therapies One of the most important questions in PSMA radiopharmaceutical development is how different isotopes behave in vivo. Lutetium177 and actinium225 differ in emission properties, tissue penetration, and potential toxicity profiles. Our comparative biodistribution analyses showed that while both agents localize to PSMA-expressing tumors, [177Lu]LuPSMA617 demonstrated more favorable tumortotissue ratios across several organs. These findings provide early insight into how isotope choice may influence therapeutic window and tolerability. While alpha-emitters remain highly compelling for their potent cytotoxicity, data like this emphasize the importance of rigorous preclinical evaluation in clinically relevant models before advancing treatment strategies. Why this approach matters for radiopharmaceutical pipelines Radiopharmaceutical development is inherently multidisciplinary, integrating chemistry, biology, imaging, and therapeutic evaluation. PDX models provide a unifying platform where all of these components can be assessed in context. Using well-characterized mCRPC PDXs allows us to: Link PSMA expression directly to in vivo uptake Compare isotopes in clinically relevant tumor models Evaluate tumor selectivity alongside therapeutic response Reduce translational uncertainty before clinical studies This kind of integrated preclinical strategy is especially valuable as PSMA-targeted therapies continue to expand into earlier disease settings and combination regimens. Want to see the full dataset? This blog highlights key findings, but the full study includes detailed radiochemistry validation, biodistribution data, tumor-to-tissue ratios, and efficacy results across multiple PDX models. Download our AACR 2026 poster to explore the complete results and analyses.

title: How to Get Leads: A Step-by-Step Guide for Startups (2026)
summary: Learn how to get leads for your B2B startup: define your ICP, pick the right channels, build and score your list, and run outbound that gets replies.
body_text: TL;DR: Getting qualified B2B leads takes four moves done in order: define your ICP, pick two or three channels that fit your team size, build and enrich a list against that ICP, then run inbound and outbound in parallel while scoring every lead before sales touches it. How to Get Leads: A Step-by-Step Guide for Startups (2026) Last updated: July 2026 Most 'how to get leads' advice lists channels and stops there. The actual bottleneck for seed-to-Series-B teams isn't which channel to try. It's running the unglamorous steps around it consistently: defining who counts as a lead, building the list, and scoring what comes in before a rep wastes time on it. Here's the process, not just the tactics list. Define What Counts as a Qualified Lead First A lead only counts if it fits who actually buys from you. Before touching any channel, define the filters that separate a real prospect from a name on a list: company size and stage, industry, tech stack, job title and seniority, and a buying signal like a recent funding round, a new GTM hire, or a tool switch. Skip this step and every number downstream gets worse. A list of thousands of names scraped with no ICP filter converts at a fraction of the rate of a few hundred contacts that match your ICP on every dimension. Write the filter down first. Every channel, list, and outbound sequence below should run against it, not around it. This also changes what "more leads" means. A seed-stage team chasing volume ends up with a CRM full of contacts nobody can sell to. The goal isn't the biggest list. It's the smallest list that reliably turns into pipeline. Pick the Channels That Fit Your Team Size Most "how to get leads" advice lists every channel available: SEO, cold email, LinkedIn outbound, paid ads, communities, partnerships, referrals. A 2-5 person GTM team can't run all of them well. Picking two or three and going deep beats spreading thin across six. SEO and content compound over time but take three to six months before they produce meaningful volume. They're worth starting early, but they shouldn't be the only channel for a team that needs pipeline this quarter. Cold outbound (email and LinkedIn) produces pipeline in weeks, not months, because you control who gets contacted and when. It's the fastest channel to test and the one most early-stage teams should run in parallel with content from day one. Paid search and paid social buy speed at the cost of margin. For most seed-to-Series-B budgets, paid works best as a supplement once a channel is already proving out, not as the first move. Communities and partnerships work well for technical or niche ICPs where trust matters more than reach, but they rarely scale as a standalone channel. Treat them as a source of warm intros, not a pipeline engine. For a full breakdown of channel-by-channel trade-offs, see The Best Lead Generation Channels for B2B Startups (2026) . The rest of this guide assumes you've picked outbound plus one other channel and walks through running them well. Build and Enrich a List Against Your ICP Once the ICP filter exists, building the list is mechanical. Pull raw contacts from a prospecting database like Apollo filtered by the firmographic and technographic criteria you defined: company size, industry, tech stack, and title. Raw pulls are noisy. A tool like Clay enriches each contact with real-time signals a static database can't capture: recent funding, new job postings, leadership changes, tool switches picked up from job listings or public integrations pages. These signals are what separate a contact who might buy from one who definitely won't right now. Score the enriched list against your ICP before it reaches outbound or sales. A simple point system works: award points for firmographic fit, more points for a live buying signal, and cut anything below a threshold instead of routing it into a sequence. Sending outbound to unscored leads is how deliverability and reply rates both quietly get worse. Dedupe against your CRM before loading anything into a sequencer. Reps re-touching accounts that are already mid-conversation with someone else on the team is a common and avoidable source of embarrassing outbound. Lists decay. Job changes, company moves, and role changes make static exports stale within months, so treat list-building as a recurring process, not a one-time export. Refresh enrichment for active accounts on a regular cadence rather than working off a list you built once. For the full list-building workflow, including where to source data and how to structure enrichment, see How to Build a Lead List in 2026: The Complete Guide . Ditch your expensive CRM subscription Get a custom CRM designed for your workflow at a fraction of the price. Talk to our team to get a fixed quote. Book a call Convert Inbound Traffic Before It Leaves SEO and content bring visitors who never fill out a form. That traffic isn't leads yet, and most of it stays invisible unless something is watching for it. Visitor identification and intent-signal tools flag which companies are on your site, which pages they viewed, and how many times they've come back. A prospect who reads your pricing page twice in a week is a different lead than someone who bounced off the homepage once. That difference matters more than raw traffic volume when deciding who gets an outbound touch this week. Route identified visitors into the same scored, enriched pipeline your outbound list runs through, rather than waiting for a form-fill that may never come. A visitor who matches your ICP and has shown a real buying signal deserves the same enrichment and scoring pass as a name pulled from Apollo. Where you do use forms, keep them short: name, email, company. Every extra field trades a percentage of completions for a data point most teams don't act on anyway. Inbound and outbound aren't competing strategies. The same ICP and scoring model should apply to both, so a lead's source doesn't determine how seriously it's treated. A well-fit inbound visitor and a well-fit outbound target should land in the same queue. For a deeper look at building the inbound side of the funnel, see Inbound Lead Generation: What It Is and How to Do It . Run Outbound That Doesn't Read Like a Template Personalization means referencing something specific to the account, not swapping in a first-name token. A recent funding round, a new GTM hire, or a tech-stack signal picked up during enrichment gives the first line a reason to exist. Generic openers get generic results: ignored or reported as spam. Use a sequencer like Instantly to schedule multi-step cadences across email and LinkedIn rather than sending a single email and moving on. Most replies come from the second, third, or fourth touch in a sequence, not the first message, so a one-and-done outreach effort undercounts what the channel can actually do. Plan for at least four touches spaced over two to three weeks, mixing channels (email, LinkedIn connection request, LinkedIn message) so the same prospect sees the outreach from more than one angle. Sending infrastructure matters as much as the copy. Warm up new sending domains gradually and stay within deliverability limits before scaling volume. A strong sequence sent from a flagged domain never reaches an inbox to begin with. Track reply rate by sequence step, not just overall. If the first touch consistently underperforms the later ones, the opener needs work before the cadence needs more steps. For a full outbound playbook, including cadence structure and channel mix, see How to Run Outbound Sales in 2026: The Complete Playbook . Score and Route Leads Before Sales Sees Them Score every lead, inbound or outbound, against the same ICP criteria defined at the start: firmographic fit, plus any live buying signal. A consistent scoring model is what makes "lead" mean the same thing across the whole team instead of a different bar for whoever generated it. Separate marketing-qualified from sales-qualified. A marketing-qualified lead fits the ICP and has shown some interest (visited the site, opened an email, engaged with content). A sales-qualified lead adds a real buying signal on top: budget, authority, or an active trigger like a recent tool switch or new hire in a relevant role. Handing marketing-qualified leads straight to reps as if they were sales-ready is a common way to burn a sales team's time and a prospect's patience. Route by score, not by order of arrival. A rep working leads first-come-first-served spends the same time on a poor-fit contact as a strong one. Routing rules that prioritize score put reps in front of the accounts most likely to close first. Track qualification-to-close rate by source. A channel that produces a lot of leads but a low qualification rate is worth reconsidering even if the raw volume looks good on a dashboard. For a full framework on building this scoring system, see B2B Lead Qualification Framework: How to Use ICP to Build Your System . Where Miniloop Fits The steps above (defining your ICP, picking channels, building a scored list, running outbound and inbound in parallel) are the strategy, and they're not hard to understand. What eats a founder's week is the busywork underneath it: scraping and enriching contact data, drafting the first version of every outreach sequence, watching for buying signals across dozens of accounts, and keeping a CRM clean enough to route leads correctly. Miniloop handles that busywork. We build and run lead-generation workflows for your team: Pull and enrich contact lists against your ICP from Apollo, Clay, and similar sources Score and route every lead using the criteria you define, so reps only see qualified accounts Draft personalized outbound sequences based on real buying signals, not generic templates Monitor hiring, funding, and tech-stack signals across your target accounts and flag the ones worth an immediate touch Keep list and CRM data enriched and deduped on an ongoing basis instead of decaying between manual exports Whether you have a GTM hire running this today, are about to make one, or are doing it yourself between product work, Miniloop handles the execution work so the strategy above actually gets run every week, not just the weeks someone has time for it. Try Miniloop or browse templates . Track Whether It's Actually Working Raw lead count is a vanity metric. Track qualified leads per month, by channel, using the scoring model from the section above. A channel producing hundreds of unqualified contacts looks busy and delivers nothing. Cost per qualified lead, not cost per contact, tells you where to put the next dollar or hour. A channel that's expensive per raw lead but cheap per qualified lead is working better than the numbers suggest at first glance, and vice versa. Time from first touch to reply, or to becoming sales-qualified, is a quality signal on its own. A list that takes a long time to produce any response usually points to weak ICP fit or weak personalization, not a channel problem. Revisit ICP criteria on a regular cadence. Buying signals shift as the market moves. Filters that reliably found buyers a while back may quietly stop working while volume still looks fine on paper. For the metrics that actually distinguish a healthy pipeline from a busy one, see Lead Generation KPIs: The Metrics That Actually Tell You If Your Pipeline Is Healthy . Related Reading Lead Generation for Startups: A Practical Guide to Building Your First Pipeline How to Build a Lead List in 2026: The Complete Guide Lead Sourcing: Strategies, Tools, and a Repeatable System for B2B Startups The Best Lead Generation Channels for B2B Startups (2026) Related Resources Get in touch - Start a low-pressure conversation with the Miniloop team Frequently Asked Questions How long does it take to start generating qualified leads? Outbound can produce qualified conversations within the first couple of weeks once your ICP and list are ready, since you control who gets contacted. SEO and content take longer, typically a few months, before they generate meaningful volume on their own. Most early-stage teams run both in parallel so outbound covers the near term while content compounds. What's the difference between a lead and a qualified lead? A lead is any contact that matches your ICP on paper: company size, industry, title, and similar filters. A qualified lead adds a real signal on top, like a funding round, a relevant new hire, or direct engagement with your content or site, that suggests they're worth a rep's time right now. Should a seed-stage startup focus on inbound or outbound first? Outbound usually comes first because it produces pipeline faster and doesn't depend on search rankings or content volume building up. Inbound (SEO and content) is worth starting at the same time since it compounds, but it shouldn't be the only channel for a team that needs leads this quarter. What tools does a small GTM team actually need to run this process? At minimum: a prospecting database like Apollo to source contacts, an enrichment tool like Clay to add buying signals, a sequencer like Instantly to run outbound cadences, and a CRM to track and route everything. Most of these tools price by usage or seat count, so a small team can start on entry-level plans and scale up as volume grows. How do I know if a lead-gen channel is actually working? Look at qualified leads and cost per qualified lead by channel, not raw contact counts or website traffic. A channel that produces a lot of unqualified names or unengaged traffic isn't working even if the top-line numbers look busy. How often should I refresh my ICP and lead list? Revisit ICP criteria on a regular cadence, since buying signals and the makeup of your best customers shift as the market moves. Refresh enrichment for active accounts more frequently than the rest of the list so contact and signal data doesn't go stale between outreach touches.

title: Life Time Expands LT Games Competition to Dallas with New HYBRID XT Studio at Frisco Club
summary: Second dedicated space supports growing demand for hybrid fitness – registration opens in July for October LT Games competition Key Highlights: Life Time is expanding its LT Games hybrid fitness...
body_text: Second dedicated space supports growing demand for hybrid fitness – registration opens in July for October LT Games competition Key Highlights: Life Time is expanding its LT Games hybrid fitness competition from Minneapolis and adding a Dallas competition October 2-3, 2026 at Life Time Frisco Registration opens July 14 for Life Time members and July 16 for non-members. $25,000 prize purse for top male and female finishers. Life Time Frisco is the second dedicated HYBRID XT studio, powering training for the fast-growing demand for hybrid fitness competitions. Minneapolis debuted in 2025. FRISCO, Texas , July 1, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Life Time (NYSE: LTH), the nation's premier healthy lifestyle brand, today announced the expansion of its elite LT Games hybrid athletic competition to North Texas, anchored by the opening of its second dedicated HYBRID XT studio at Life Time Frisco . The first location debuted in 2025 at Life Time Target Center in Minneapolis. The Frisco location will host the upcoming LT Games Dallas competition on October 2-3, 2026, bringing the competitive format to a new market. Registration will open with limited availability for 144 athletes, with Life Time members gaining early access on July 14 and non-members on July 16. The event will feature a $25,000 prize purse, with top male and female finishers earning prize money and prize packages. Demand for hybrid-style training continues to accelerate, as highlighted by the American College of Sports Medicine's 2026 Worldwide Fitness Trends report , which ranks functional fitness among the year's top trends. LT Games is built to address this demand, giving athletes flexibility in how they complete each exercise. Since launching the format, Life Time has seen strong athlete response and rising registration demand, driving the expansion to new locations. "Hybrid fitness continues to gain a ton of momentum as athletes look for ways to keep pushing the envelope with strength and endurance. We've seen a ton of demand and positive response from athletes for our two LT Games competitions at Target Center," said Wes Robertson, LT Games Race Director at Life Time. "With the addition of our Frisco HYBRID XT studio and the expansion of LT Games into Dallas, we're just getting started growing our options for members to break through barriers." Designed as a regular format for hybrid athletes, HYBRID XT delivers structured, coach-led programming that prepares participants for the LT Games and everyday performance. HYBRID XT classes blend: Conditioning and endurance with running, rowing and SkiErg work Functional strength with barbells, dumbbells, sleds and bodyweight training Athletic movement patterns including pushing, pulling, carrying and rotational work As hybrid fitness continues to evolve, Life Time is uniquely positioned at the intersection of training, community and competition, offering a seamless journey from daily workouts to national competition platforms. Beyond LT Games, Life Time delivers nearly 30 athletic events nationwide , from gravel cycling to running, giving members opportunities to set goals, challenge themselves and take part in best-in-class experiences. With the opening of the Frisco studio, Life Time continues to scale HYBRID XT as a key component of its Signature Group Training portfolio, reinforcing its commitment to helping members discover what's possible through progressive, performance-driven programming. LT Games Dallas Competition Details: The Dallas-area competition will bring together athletes from across the country to test their performance across a series of strength and cardio-based challenges. Dates: October 2–3, 2026 Location: Life Time Frisco Registration: Members: $249 opens July 14, 2026 Non-members: $299 opens July 16, 2026 Prize purse: $25,000 LT Games debuted in Minneapolis in October 2025 followed by a second competition in April 2026, drawing top hybrid competitors like Lauren Weeks and Dylan Scott. To learn more on registration, visit the LT Games website . You can also learn more about the movements in the competition in this Experience Life magazine article . For more information about Life Time, visit www.lifetime.life , follow on social media at Facebook , Instagram and LinkedIn , or download the Life Time app. You can also find Life Time's collection of supplements, equipment and apparel on the LT Shop by following its Instagram page . About Life Time Life Time (NYSE: LTH) empowers people to live healthy, happy lives through its more than 190 athletic country clubs across the U.S. and Canada, the complimentary and comprehensive Life Time app featuring its L•AI•C™ AI-powered health companion, and more than 30 iconic athletic events. Serving people ages 90 days to 90+ years, the Life Time ecosystem uniquely delivers healthy living, healthy aging, and healthy entertainment experiences, a range of unique healthy way of life programs, highly trusted LTH nutritional supplements and more. Recognized as a Great Place to Work®, the company is committed to upholding an exceptional culture for its more than 50,000 team members. SOURCE Life Time, Inc.

title: Die Streckgrenze verstehen
summary: Erfahren Sie, was Streckgrenze ist, warum sie für Ingenieure wichtig ist und wie sie gemessen wird. Vergleichen Sie Werkstoffe und sehen Sie, wie sich die Streckgrenze auf die Konstruktion in der Praxis auswirkt.
body_text: Das Verständnis der Streckgrenze ist eine echte Stärke, die Ihnen einen Vorteil in der Fertigung verschafft. Stellen Sie sich vor, Sie biegen eine Büroklammer. Zuerst springt sie zurück, dann bleibt sie plötzlich gebogen. Dieser Übergangspunkt ist die Streckgrenze. Für Ingenieure, die alles von Flugzeugflügeln bis hin zu medizinischen Geräten konstruieren, ist dies eine der wichtigsten Materialeigenschaften, die es zu verstehen gilt. Was ist Streckgrenze Die Streckgrenze ist die Belastungsschwelle, bei der Materialien von elastischem Verhalten (reversible Verformung) zu plastischem Verhalten (dauerhafte Verformung) übergehen. Sie wird in Megapascal (MPa) gemessen und definiert, wie viel Belastung ein Material aushalten kann, ohne seine ursprüngliche Form zu verlieren. Ingenieure nutzen Daten zur Streckgrenze, um zu überprüfen, ob Bauteile ihre Lasten tragen können, ohne sich zu verbiegen oder zu brechen. Wichtige Zusammenhänge bei der Streckgrenze Es gibt einige grundlegende Zusammenhänge, die Kraft, Verformung und Steifigkeit miteinander verbinden. Diese bilden das Rückgrat dafür, wie Ingenieure die Streckgrenze definieren und berechnen. Spannung ( σ): Stellen Sie sich Spannung als die Kraft pro Fläche vor, die auf ein Material wirkt. Die Formel lautet σ = F/A, wobei F die aufgebrachte Kraft und A die Querschnittsfläche ist. Wenn Sie auf eine kleinere Fläche stärker drücken, steigt die Spannung. Dehnung (ε): Die Dehnung misst, um wie viel sich etwas im Vergleich zu seiner ursprünglichen Größe ausdehnt oder zusammenpresst. Formel: ε = ΔL/L₀, wobei Δ L die Längenänderung und L₀ die Ausgangslänge ist. Sie gibt im Grunde an, um wie viel sich das Material gedehnt hat. Elastizitätsmodul (E) : Dieser gibt an, wie steif ein Material ist. Er ist das Verhältnis von Spannung zu Dehnung (E = σ/ε ) im elastischen Bereich. Ein hoher E-Wert bedeutet, dass sich das Material unter Belastung kaum verformt, wie beispielsweise Stahl im Vergleich zu Gummi. Hookesches Gesetz : Im elastischen Bereich steigen Spannung und Dehnung linear zueinander an: σ = E × ε . Diese Regel gilt bis zum Erreichen der Streckgrenze; danach knickt die Kurve ab und das Material beginnt, sich dauerhaft zu verformen. Spannungs-Dehnungs-Kurve : Diese Grafik fasst alle Zusammenhänge zusammen und stellt die Spannung (vertikal) der Dehnung (horizontal) gegenüber, während ein Material belastet wird. Zunächst ist die Linie gerade und stellt die Eigenschaften einer Feder dar, bei der das Material zurückspringt, wenn man es loslässt. Wenn die Linie anfängt, sich zu krümmen, ist das die Streckgrenze. Danach nimmt das Material dauerhafte Formveränderungen an, wie eine Büroklammer, die verbogen bleibt. Diese Biegung in der Kurve definiert die Streckgrenze. Ein steifes Material (hoher E-Wert) widersteht Verformungen, was jedoch nicht immer bedeutet, dass es eine hohe Streckgrenze aufweist. Die besten technischen Werkstoffe bieten ein ausgewogenes Verhältnis zwischen Steifigkeit und Festigkeit, je nachdem, welche Anforderungen an das Bauteil gestellt werden. Warum die Streckgrenze in der Fertigung wichtig ist Die Streckgrenze ist für Ingenieure eine entscheidende Konstruktionsgrenze. Sie ist die Grenze, die bestimmt, ob Ihre Bauteile unter den zu erwartenden Belastungen zuverlässig funktionieren oder sich dauerhaft verformen. Sicherheit einbauen: In der Praxis bringen Ingenieure Materialien nicht annähernd an ihre Streckgrenze. Stattdessen dimensionieren sie für etwa 25–50 % dieser Grenze und lassen so eine Sicherheitsmarge für unerwartete Belastungen und Abweichungen in der Praxis. Vermeidung von Versagen in großen Strukturen : Bei Brücken oder Flugzeugflügeln bleibt ein Bauteil, sobald es nachgibt, verbogen. Das stellt eine unmittelbare Gefahr dar. Die Streckgrenze hilft Ingenieuren dabei, vorherzusagen, wann diese Veränderung eintritt. Auswahl des richtigen Materials: Unterschiedliche Anwendungen erfordern unterschiedliche Streckgrenzen. In der Luft- und Raumfahrt werden häufig Titanlegierungen (800–1200 MPa) verwendet, während ABS-Kunststoff (~45 MPa) sich gut für Elektronikgehäuse eignet. Abwägen von Kosten und Leistung: Stärkere Materialien ermöglichen leichtere Konstruktionen, sind jedoch in der Regel teurer und schwieriger zu verarbeiten. Daten zur Streckgrenze helfen dabei, Leistung, Gewicht und Budget in Einklang zu bringen. Schutz vor Ermüdung: Wiederholte Belastungen nahe der Streckgrenze schwächen Materialien langsam. Eine Auslegung deutlich unterhalb der Streckgrenze verlängert die Lebensdauer und verhindert langfristige Ermüdungsschäden. Das Verständnis von Materialeigenschaften wie der Streckgrenze ist für eine effektive Materialauswahl von grundlegender Bedeutung und hilft Ingenieuren, Leistung, Kosten und Herstellbarkeit in Einklang zu bringen. Verfahren zur Bestimmung der Streckgrenze Die genaue Messung der Streckgrenze hängt von der Verwendung der richtigen Prüfverfahren ab, die je nach Material und Konstruktionsanforderungen variieren. Hier sind die wichtigsten, auf die sich Ingenieure stützen: Zugversuch (0,2 %-Offset-Methode): Dies ist die Standardmethode für Metalle. Wenn auf der Spannungs-Dehnungs-Kurve keine klare Streckgrenze erkennbar ist, ziehen Ingenieure eine Linie mit einem Versatz von 0,2 % Dehnung, um die Streckgrenze zu definieren. Zugversuche an 3D-Druckmaterialien zeigen, wie die additive Fertigung zusätzliche Herausforderungen mit sich bringt, da sich gedruckte Teile in verschiedenen Richtungen unterschiedlich verhalten können. Härtekorrelation: Härtetests sind schnell und praktisch. Sie werden in der Produktion häufig eingesetzt, um die Streckgrenze für Qualitätskontrollen oder die Eingangskontrolle von Materialien abzuschätzen. Bei der Materialhärteprüfung wird untersucht, wie verschiedene Härteskalen mit Festigkeitswerten in Verbindung gebracht werden können. Prüfspannungsversuche: Bei Polymeren und Verbundwerkstoffen, die nicht immer eine klare Streckgrenze aufweisen, erfassen Ingenieure stattdessen die Spannung bei einer geringen Dehnung (z. B. 0,1 % oder 0,2 %) und verwenden diese als Streckgrenze. Dies bietet eine einfache Möglichkeit, Materialien zu vergleichen und zu konstruieren, die sich langsamer biegen oder dehnen. Streckgrenze nach Fertigungstechnologie Die Art der Herstellung eines Bauteils hat großen Einfluss auf dessen Streckgrenze. Der Prozess kann die innere Struktur des Materials verändern und sogar Eigenspannungen hinterlassen, die dessen Verhalten unter Belastung beeinflussen. Deshalb ist es wichtig, neben der Materialauswahl auch die Fertigungsmethoden zu berücksichtigen. CNC-Bearbeitung Das Schneiden kann die Oberfläche von Metallen leicht verhärten, was die Festigkeit in einigen Bereichen erhöhen kann. Aluminiumlegierungen (40–400 MPa) lassen sich leicht bearbeiten, können jedoch in der Nähe scharfer Kanten Festigkeitsänderungen aufweisen. Stähle (250+ MPa) sind gleichmäßiger, weisen jedoch oft Eigenspannungen auf, die berücksichtigt werden müssen. Bei der Materialauswahl muss abgewogen werden, wie sich Bearbeitbarkeit und Festigkeit in Einklang bringen lassen. Spritzguss Bei Kunststoffen ist die Verarbeitung genauso wichtig wie das Material selbst. ABS kann unter den richtigen Bedingungen im Spritzgussverfahren eine Festigkeit von ca. 40–50 MPa erreichen, während Polypropylen mit ca. 30–35 MPa etwas weniger fest ist, dafür aber eine gute chemische Beständigkeit aufweist. Wissenschaftliche Spritzgussprinzipien zeigen, wie die Steuerung von Temperatur, Druck und Kühlung zu gleichmäßigeren Ergebnissen führt. 3D-Druck Gedruckte Teile verhalten sich je nach Art des Schichtaufbaus unterschiedlich. PA12-Nylon kann ~45 MPa erreichen, während DMLS-Aluminiumlegierungen (AlSi10Mg) ~230 MPa erreichen können, ähnlich wie geschmiedetes Aluminium. Ausrichtung, Schichtdicke und Nachbearbeitung machen einen großen Unterschied. Die Wahl des Materials für additive Verfahren spielt ebenfalls eine wichtige Rolle bei der Streckgrenze, wie im Leitfaden zu 3D-Druckmaterialien von Protolabs erläutert. Vergleich der Streckgrenze verschiedener Materialien Die Materialauswahl legt die Grenzen dessen fest, was ein Design leisten kann. Das Verständnis der Streckgrenzeigenschaften hilft Ingenieuren, fundierte Kompromisse einzugehen und die optimale Leistung für ihre Teile zu erzielen. Metalle : Metalle sind für ihre höchsten Streckgrenzen bekannt und daher die erste Wahl für strukturelle Anwendungen. Sie bieten Zuverlässigkeit unter hoher Belastung, erhöhen jedoch das Gewicht und können die Kosten steigern. Ingenieure wägen bei der Wahl zwischen Stahl, Aluminium oder Titan oft das Verhältnis von Festigkeit zu Gewicht ab. Kunststoffe : Sie weisen deutlich niedrigere Streckgrenzen als Metalle auf, bieten jedoch Gestaltungsfreiheit, geringes Gewicht und einfache Verarbeitung. Kunststoffe eignen sich gut für Gehäuse, Einfassungen und Teile mit geringer Belastung, bei denen Geometrie und Kosteneffizienz wichtiger sind als reine Festigkeit. Elastomere : Im Vergleich zu Metallen und Kunststoffen extrem niedrige Streckgrenzen, doch ihr Wert liegt in ihrer Elastizität. Sie kehren nach Dehnung in ihre ursprüngliche Form zurück, was sie für Dichtungen, Dichtungsringe und schwingungsdämpfende Teile unverzichtbar macht. Verbundwerkstoffe: Verbundwerkstoffe sind in bestimmten Richtungen fest und insgesamt leicht und bieten ein ausgezeichnetes Verhältnis von Festigkeit zu Gewicht. Ihre Leistungsfähigkeit hängt stark von der Faserausrichtung und der Verarbeitung ab, weshalb eine sorgfältige Konstruktion entscheidend ist. Carbon-DLS-Materialien bieten technische Harzeigenschaften für Anwendungen, die eine verbundwerkstoffähnliche Leistungsfähigkeit erfordern. Vergleich der Materialeigenschaften Material Streckgrenze (MPa) Dichte (g/cm³) Festigkeits-Gewichts-Verhältnis Herstellungsverfahren Aluminium 6061-T6 276 2.7 102 CNC-Bearbeitung Steel 1045 310 7.8 40 CNC-Bearbeitung Titanium Ti-6Al-4V 880 4.4 200 CNC-Bearbeitung / 3D-Druck ABS 45 1 45 Spritzguss Polypropylene 32 0.9 36 Spritzguss PEEK 90 1.3 69 Spritzguss Liquid Silicone Rubber (LSR 60A) 5 1.1 5 Spritzguss TPU (Thermoplastic Polyurethane) 12 1.2 10 Spritzguss TPE (Thermoplastic Elastomer) 8 1 8 Spritzguss PA12 Nylon (SLS) 45 1 45 3D-Druck Aluminium AlSi10Mg (DMLS) 230 2.7 85 3D-Druck Carbon EPX 82 84 1.2 70 3D-Druck (Carbon DLS) Die Werte sind typisch, die tatsächlichen Ergebnisse hängen jedoch von den Verarbeitungsbedingungen, der Wärmebehandlung und den Prüfnormen ab. Faktoren, die die Streckgrenze beeinflussen Die Streckgrenze ist nicht konstant. Sie ändert sich in Abhängigkeit von Umgebungsbedingungen, Verarbeitungsgeschichte und Belastungsmerkmalen. Temperatur: Wärme verändert die Materialfestigkeit. Stähle können bei etwa 200 °C etwa 20 % ihrer Festigkeit verlieren. Kunststoffe können schnell erweichen, sobald sie ihre Glasübergangstemperatur überschreiten. Einige Materialien werden bei Kälte auch spröde, selbst wenn ihre Festigkeitswerte auf dem Papier hoch erscheinen. Dehnungsgeschwindigkeit: Die Geschwindigkeit der Belastung beeinflusst das Verhalten. Ein schneller Aufprall kann manche Materialien stärker erscheinen lassen, da sie unter schneller Belastung vorübergehend einer Verformung widerstehen. Diese scheinbare Festigkeit kann jedoch irreführend sein, da das Material die Energie möglicherweise nicht absorbiert und stattdessen reißen oder zerbrechen kann, was zu einem plötzlichen Versagen führt. Dies ist ein entscheidender Faktor bei Anwendungen wie Crash-Sicherheitsteilen oder Schutzausrüstung. Zusammensetzung und Wärmebehandlung: Die Anpassung der chemischen Zusammensetzung, beispielsweise durch Zugabe von Kohlenstoff zu Stahl, kann die Streckgrenze erheblich verändern. Wärmebehandlungen können je nach Verfahren und Konstruktionsanforderungen die Zähigkeit erhöhen oder die Härte verringern. Auswirkungen der Fertigung : Fertigungsprozesse hinterlassen oft Spuren. Kaltumformung, maschinelle Bearbeitung und Formgebung können verborgene Spannungen im Material einschließen und die Anordnung seiner inneren Struktur verändern. Je nach Geometrie und Verfahren kann dies die Leistung entweder verbessern oder verringern. Konstruktionsüberlegungen auf Basis der Streckgrenze Um Daten zur Streckgrenze in zuverlässige Konstruktionsentscheidungen umzusetzen, müssen Sicherheitsfaktoren, Spannungskonzentrationen und Umwelteinflüsse verstanden werden. Sicherheitsfaktoren Ingenieure wenden Faktoren von 1,5–4× an, je nachdem, wie kritisch die Anwendung ist. Das bedeutet, dass ein Bauteil so ausgelegt ist, dass es Lasten tragen kann, die um ein Vielfaches höher sind als erwartet, wodurch eine Sicherheitsmarge für Unwägbarkeiten bei der Materialqualität, Lastschwankungen oder Betriebsbedingungen eingebaut wird. Luft- und Raumfahrtstrukturen benötigen in der Regel höhere Faktoren (3–4×), da ein Versagen schwerwiegende Folgen hat, während bei Konsumgütern niedrigere Faktoren (1,5–2×) verwendet werden können, um die Kosten niedrig zu halten. Spannungskonzentrationen Spannungen an bestimmten Stellen – wie Löchern, Kerben oder scharfen Ecken – können 3- bis 5-mal höher sein als die durchschnittliche Spannung im restlichen Material. Selbst wenn die Gesamtbelastung sicher erscheint, können diese Spannungsherde das Bauteil über die Streckgrenze hinaus belasten und Risse oder bleibende Verformungen verursachen. Glattere Übergänge und Verrundungen verteilen die Spannung und verringern das Risiko. Einhaltung von Normen Industrienormen legen Mindeststreckgrenzen und Prüfverfahren fest. Beispiele hierfür sind ASTM A36 für Baustahl (mindestens 250 MPa), ISO 898-1 für Schrauben, ASTM D638 für Kunststoffe und AS9100 für die Luft- und Raumfahrt. Umwelteinflüsse Reale Umgebungsbedingungen wie Hitze, Feuchtigkeit, UV-Strahlung und Chemikalien können die effektive Streckgrenze um 20–50 % verringern. Die Einwirkung von Witterungseinflüssen kann Polymere langsam zersetzen, Metalle korrodieren oder Verbundwerkstoffe spröde machen. Konstrukteure müssen dies berücksichtigen und Schutzbeschichtungen, die Materialauswahl oder Umweltprüfungen in Betracht ziehen. Fertigungstoleranzen Die tatsächliche Festigkeit hängt davon ab, wie das Bauteil hergestellt wird. Wärmebehandlung, Oberflächenbeschaffenheit und Maßgenauigkeit können die Leistung im Vergleich zum Datenblatt verändern. Bei der Konstruktion für die Fertigung ist es wichtig, diese Abweichungen zu berücksichtigen und Sicherheitsmargen einzuplanen, damit das Bauteil wie vorgesehen funktioniert. Branchen, in denen die Streckgrenze entscheidend ist Verschiedene Branchen sind mit sehr unterschiedlichen Belastungen und Risiken konfrontiert, sodass die Streckgrenze je nach Anwendung eine unterschiedliche Rolle spielt. Hier sind einige Branchen, die eine äußerst präzise Streckgrenze erfordern . Luft- und Raumfahrt Hier zählt jedes Kilogramm. Flugzeuge und Raumfahrzeuge benötigen Werkstoffe mit dem höchsten Verhältnis von Festigkeit zu Gewicht. Deshalb sind Titanlegierungen (wie Ti-6Al-4V, 800–1200 MPa) und Kohlefaserverbundwerkstoffe so weit verbreitet. Beispiele: Flugzeugrümpfe, Fahrwerke, Turbinenschaufeln und Satelliten. Anwendungen, bei denen Zuverlässigkeit entscheidend ist. Automobil Autos müssen Unfälle sicher bewältigen. Hochfeste Stähle (400–800 MPa) sind auf Knautschzonen und Verstärkungen abgestimmt, damit sie sich kontrolliert verformen und Energie absorbieren. Beispiele: Knautschzonen, Querlenker, Fahrwerksteile und Überrollkäfige. Medizin Chirurgische Instrumente und Implantate stehen vor unterschiedlichen Herausforderungen. Einige werden nur einmal verwendet, während andere im Körper Millionen von Zyklen durchlaufen. Rostfreie Stähle (~200–300 MPa) und Titanlegierungen sind die erste Wahl. Beispiele: Hüft- und Kniegelenkersatz, Knochenschrauben, Zahnimplantate und chirurgische Instrumente, die wiederholter Sterilisation standhalten müssen. Industrieausrüstung Schwerlastmaschinen sind ständig im Einsatz, oft unter rauen Umgebungsbedingungen. Die verwendeten Materialien müssen robust und langlebig sein, auch bei hohen Temperaturen. Beispiele: Zahnräder, Wellen, Kräne, Druckbehälter, Rohrleitungen und Bergbaumaschinen, bei denen Ausfälle enorme Kosten und Ausfallzeiten bedeuten. FAQ Was ist der Unterschied zwischen Streckgrenze und Zugfestigkeit? expand_less expand_more Die Streckgrenze ist der Punkt, an dem ein Material beginnt, sich dauerhaft zu verformen oder zu dehnen. Die Zugfestigkeit ist die maximale Belastung, die es aushalten kann, bevor es bricht. Bei Metallen beträgt die Streckgrenze in der Regel etwa 60–90 % der Zugfestigkeit. Wie wird die Streckgrenze gemessen? expand_less expand_more Sie wird in der Regel mit einem Zugversuch gemessen. Wenn das Material keine klare Streckgrenze aufweist, verwenden Ingenieure häufig die 0,2 %-Offset-Methode, um diese zu bestimmen. Warum variiert die Streckgrenze bei 3D-gedruckten Teilen? expand_less expand_more Da beim 3D-Druck Teile Schicht für Schicht aufgebaut werden, hängt die Festigkeit von der Ausrichtung ab. Belastungen, die quer über die Schichten wirken, können die Streckgrenze um 20–40 % verringern, da die Verbindung zwischen den Schichten schwächer ist. Kann die Streckgrenze nach der Herstellung verändert werden? expand_less expand_more Ja. Verfahren wie Wärmebehandlung, Kaltverfestigung oder Oberflächenbehandlungen können Materialien deutlich fester machen. Je nach Material sind Veränderungen von 50–200 % möglich. Wie wirken sich Temperaturänderungen auf die Streckgrenze aus? expand_less expand_more Viele Metalle verlieren bei steigender Temperatur merklich an Festigkeit. Stähle können beispielsweise bei 200 °C bis zu ~20 % ihrer Festigkeit einbüßen. Kunststoffe reagieren noch empfindlicher, insbesondere wenn sie sich ihrer Glasübergangstemperatur nähern. title: Tuya Smart Powers the Next Wave of AI Toys at Spielwarenmesse 2026 | news | Tuya Smart
body_text: NUREMBERG – Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA, HKEX: 2391), a global AI cloud platform service provider, showcased a series of groundbreaking AI products at Spielwarenmesse 2026 in Nuremberg from January 27 to 31. At the event, Tuya also unveiled the secret behind the next generation of AI toys that are set to become the next big hit. NebulaPals Plush AI Toy The most impressive feature of the NebulaPals Plush AI Toy is its real-time LED facial expression feedback based on user emotions. When you're happy or sad, it can respond through changes in its eyes. It not only supports smooth conversation but also features carefully designed tactile feedback, responding to hugs and touches vividly. Combined with storytelling, news broadcasting, and interactive games, it becomes a true AI companion with long-term memory and emotional companionship capabilities. Walulu Walulu precisely addresses the demand for personalized companionship. Its AI core can detect up to 19 distinct emotional responses and supports over 60 languages. Moreover, it integrates seamlessly with major AI large language models, including ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Doubao. Users can choose or cultivate a range of personality traits—such as cheerful, quiet, curious, or considerate—to build a personalized, dynamic pet community. AI Learning Camera The AI Learning Camera skillfully blends AI vision with education. Its object recognition feature not only identifies objects but also links them to cultural and educational content. For example, when capturing foreign languages, the camera can provide real-time pronunciation and translation. Additionally, its built-in AI filters and image transformation features can turn children’s doodles into stunning digital artwork, igniting creativity. Through multimodal AI conversations, it can also become a fun, exploratory companion for children as they discover the world. In addition, Tuya showcased AI robotic dogs with motion mimicry and emotional interaction capabilities, responding to voice commands and performing a variety of realistic actions. There was also the AI Clock, offering customizable theme scenes and alarm settings that turn every wake-up into a ceremonial experience. These innovative AI products represent the expanding boundaries of intelligent companionship. They demonstrate that the next generation of AI toys is moving beyond single-function toys to offer deeper emotional resonance, more personalized interactive experiences, and seamless integration with real-world scenarios. Tuya AI Toy Solution: The Foundation Behind Hot-Selling Products Developing truly intelligent AI toys is no easy task. From hardware design and AI model training to multilingual support and content safety, every step presents a unique challenge. To empower developers, brands, and retailers to create the next generation of AI toys, Tuya Smart introduced its comprehensive AI toy solution at the Spielwarenmesse 2026. The solution spans the entire process—from concept design and hardware/software development to AI personality creation and market launch—dramatically reducing the development and application barriers for AI toys. Transform Toys to AI Companions Using Tuya’s AI Agent Development Platform, customers can design the personality, memory logic, and behavioral patterns of their toys without having to train underlying models or build complex infrastructure. The platform seamlessly integrates with leading AI models, enabling multi-turn conversations, emotional feedback, and scenario-based memory, effectively transforming static toys into intelligent, responsive companions that can connect more deeply with users. Flexible AI Toy Development Tailored to Every Client Tuya offers several development pathways to meet the various needs of brand owners and retailers. Clients can choose from ready-to-market OEM solutions, integrate AI capabilities into existing products through Tuya’s AI Modules and AI Boxes while maintaining their original design, or opt for deep customization to craft unique AI toys based on brand IP and cultural stories. Whether it's plush toys, robots, educational tools, or wearable tech, Tuya’s AI toy solutions offer the most appropriate options. Responsible Companionship Designed for Families in the AI Era Data privacy and content security are critical when it comes to children. Tuya’s AI toy solutions are equipped with a parental management app, enabling parents to monitor conversation histories, receive AI-generated behavior summaries, and gain growth insights. Parents can also manage interaction content and screen time, ensuring a responsible and secure AI companionship experience for families. Enabling Client Success Through Efficient AI Toy Deployment In the wave of AI toy innovation, Tuya provides developers, brand owners, and retailers with a faster, more cost-effective, and secure path to market. With Tuya's robust AI platform and module support, customers can bypass the complexity of building AI from scratch, reducing the development cycle from concept to mass production by more than 60%. The time to market can be as short as 15 days, enabling a fast track for launching new products. Cost-wise, Tuya’s integrated AI platform minimizes repetitive development and integration costs, leading to a 30% to 50% reduction in overall R&D and implementation expenses. On the security and compliance front, the platform is pre-configured with security frameworks that adhere to global standards like GDPR and CCPA, supporting hardware encryption, data localization, and parental controls to help products enter global markets swiftly. Additionally, Tuya's AIoT infrastructure spans over 200 countries and regions, offering real-time language support in more than 60 languages and robust cloud management capabilities, enabling efficient global deployment and operations. As AI continues to evolve, the true value of toys lies not just in their "intelligence" but in how they foster emotional connections and support growth. At the Spielwarenmesse 2026, Tuya’s showcase was more than just a presentation—it was a deeper conversation about the future of AI and emotional companionship. Looking ahead, Tuya will continue to partner with global innovators to explore the future of AI toys, creating truly warm companions for the next generation.

title: Executive Engagement, Value-Based Selling and the Future of Customer Partnerships
summary: Technology companies have traditionally built relationships through engineering teams and technical experts.
body_text: By Christine Blinn, Marketing Director Technology companies have traditionally built relationships through engineering teams and technical experts. Those connections remain essential, but as customers’ organizations become more complex and innovation cycles accelerate, successful partnerships increasingly require engagement across multiple levels of the organization. That reality was on display at the North American Manufacturing Excellence Summit (NAMES) conference, where our commercial teams applied a different approach to customer engagement: one focused on executive relationships, value-based selling and coordinated account-based marketing. The strategy reflects a broader shift happening across advanced technology industries. Moving Conversations Upstream Many sales conversations begin when a customer has already identified a specific project or technical requirement. Executive engagement creates opportunities to participate earlier in the decision-making process. At NAMES, discussions focused on innovation priorities, manufacturing strategies, automation investments and long-term business goals. Rather than leading with product specifications, conversations centered on customer outcomes and enterprise challenges. This creates opportunities to identify broader collaboration possibilities and align technology investments with strategic objectives. Connecting Technology to Business Outcomes Today’s customers are not simply evaluating products. They are evaluating business impact. That reality is driving greater adoption of value-based selling methodologies across advanced manufacturing and medical technology markets. By focusing on customer outcomes, including productivity improvements, operational efficiency, innovation enablement and competitive differentiation, organizations can create more meaningful conversations that extend beyond individual products. The result is a stronger foundation for long-term partnerships. The Power of Account-Based Marketing Another key takeaway from NAMES was the importance of coordinated engagement. Successful customer relationships rarely develop through a single interaction. They are built through multiple touchpoints across digital channels, events, thought leadership and direct conversations. At NAMES, targeted account-based marketing efforts helped create awareness and engagement with priority organizations before the event, enabling more productive conversations when attendees arrived. When marketing, business development, product management and sales work together, organizations can deliver a more consistent and relevant customer experience. Building Long-Term Partnerships The most valuable outcome from executive engagement is often not an immediate sale. It is the opportunity to establish relationships with leaders who influence innovation strategies and investment decisions, as well as long-term business direction. Those relationships help organizations identify opportunities across multiple applications, business units and technologies while creating stronger foundations for collaboration. As industries continue to evolve, companies that successfully combine technical expertise with strategic business engagement will be best positioned to create lasting value for customers and drive sustainable growth.

title: AI alone won't transform your business. Your people will.
summary: "Nobody made an outstanding wine shaving hours off the fermentation cycle." Why a room of executives stopped talking about efficiency and started talking about people.
body_text: "What happens when you stop chasing efficiency and start designing for effectiveness?" That's the question a room full of senior executives tackled on June 16, 2026, at a Zoom Executive Community Meetup in partnership with Chief Wine Officer. Over fine wine and frank conversation, leaders from global brands explored how AI can elevate human potential rather than simply replace it. The farmer's wisdom: rethinking what AI is really for Benedetto Conversano, executive advisor at Zoom, opened the evening with a Zen parable about a farmer who greets every twist of fate with the same words: "Maybe so, maybe not." His point landed immediately. We can't use old patterns to redesign a better future. We're overindexing on efficiency at the expense of effectiveness in the AI adoption race. Technology can save time, sure. The real question is what we do with that reclaimed capacity. "Efficiency has a floor, while effectiveness has no ceiling," Benedetto said. "Nobody made an outstanding wine shaving hours off the fermentation cycle." The true value of AI, he argued, isn't in the hours saved. It's in how those hours get redeployed to create new value, deepen relationships, and solve problems we couldn't tackle before. Most digital transformation initiatives have failed precisely because they optimized for speed without rethinking outcomes. Could AI actually improve quality of life at work? Benedetto thinks so. Fear, though, kills the creative thinking needed to design a better future. If we let it dominate the transformation, we lose the mental power to imagine something different. The room responded immediately. Executives shared stories of automation projects that delivered speed gains yet failed to move the business forward. The gap between efficiency and effectiveness was familiar territory for everyone. From efficiency to human elevation Laura Ball, global CX AI sales and GTM lead at Zoom, picked up the thread with a direct challenge: technology doesn't transform businesses. People do. With characteristic Yorkshire candor (tempered, she joked, by sticking to water to avoid "oversharing"), Laura pushed the audience past efficiency metrics toward what she called "effectiveness levers." Five human capabilities AI can amplify Laura outlined five distinctly human strengths that define the next era of transformation: Empathy. Using freed-up time to truly listen to customers. Curiosity. Mining new insights from every interaction. Creativity. Designing new services, not just faster ones. Proactivity. Reaching out before customers realize they need help. Redeployment. Transforming agents into analysts, designers, and experience architects. Transformation stories from the field Drawing on a decade of redesigning operations across industries, Laura shared examples that brought the theory to life. In financial services, customer service agents were upskilled into AI agent designers and builders. These roles didn't exist before. Now they're industry standard. In retail, store associates became digital stylists, connecting with customers remotely while driving incremental revenue. In the public sector, teams freed from administrative tasks were redirected to provide emotional support for people in financial difficulty. These weren't technology implementations. They were human redesign stories. Each began with a simple question: "What could this person do if we freed them from the repetitive?" The debate: measuring what matters Following the presentations, the room erupted into animated discussion. Leaders debated how to measure human-centered ROI, how to build psychological safety for teams navigating change, and how to make the case for empathy and creativity in traditional business frameworks. Common themes emerged across the conversations: Quantifying the value of empathy and creativity remains difficult in traditional business cases. Leadership courage is essential to redesign work rather than simply automate it. New frameworks are needed that measure effectiveness, not just efficiency. Purpose and a sense of ownership are critical to successful AI adoption. Three invitations for leaders Laura closed with three invitations that resonated across the room: Reframe ROI . Stop asking "What can we cut?" and start asking "What can we create?" Redesign work . Don't just automate tasks. Elevate people by building roles around human strengths. Reimagine leadership . Lead with curiosity, not certainty. Design for possibility rather than predictability. An unexpected coronation As the formal presentations concluded, the discussions continued, as did the wine tasting. Valerie Sitterlin, Director of Enterprise AI Transformation at Elsevier, demonstrated exceptional wine knowledge and expertise, impressing both the Wine Host and fellow executives. In recognition, she was ceremoniously crowned Chief Wine Officer for the evening, a playful acknowledgment that human capabilities extend far beyond our professional domains! Continue the conversation Niall Carter, major and enterprise sales manager, UK&I at Zoom, closed the evening by emphasizing our commitment to building a thriving executive community across EMEA. A space where leaders connect, share challenges, and collectively reimagine what's possible when technology serves human potential. If you're interested in joining future conversations like this one, visit the Zoom Executive Community page to learn more. We're hosting upcoming Table Talks that dig deeper into these themes, from measuring human-centered ROI to building transformation-ready cultures. These intimate, peer-to-peer sessions are designed for senior leaders who want to move beyond the hype and into practical, human-centered AI transformation. The Chief Wine Officer's final wisdom : Just as great wine requires patience, the right conditions, and an understanding that you can't rush the process, true transformation requires us to create the conditions for human potential to flourish. Trust that the results will be worth the wait. Frequently asked questions What is the Zoom Executive Community? It's a peer network for senior leaders across EMEA. title: May 2026 U.S. National Consumer Credit Trends Report
summary: Highlights: As of May 2026, total U.S. consumer debt climbed to $18.23 trillion — a 2.4% year-over-year increase — with mortgage debt accounting for the vast majority
body_text: Insight May 2026 U.S. National Consumer Credit Trends Report July 02, 2026 Highlights: As of May 2026, total U.S. consumer debt climbed to $18.23 trillion — a 2.4% year-over-year increase — with mortgage debt accounting for the vast majority (74.2%) of that total. Non-mortgage consumer debt reached $4.7 trillion, with auto loans and leases comprising 36.4% and bankcard balances rising 3.7% to $1.1 trillion, signaling continued reliance on credit products. As of May 2026, the monthly Equifax Consumer Credit Trends Report showed that total U.S. consumer debt was $18.23 trillion, up 2.4% from May 2025. Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.52 trillion, a 74.2% share of total consumer debt, while non-mortgage consumer debt totaled $4.7 trillion, with 36.4% of non-mortgage consumer debt attributable to auto loans and leases, and 27.5% attributable to student loans. Outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 2.4% from May 2025, to $1.71 trillion in May 2026. Outstanding balances on U.S. bankcards increased versus the prior month to $1.1 trillion in May 2026, up 3.7% from May 2025. Average bankcard utilization stood at 20.3%, which is a slight decrease from 20.7% in May 2025. Stay Ahead in the Evolving Credit Environment Identify new growth opportunities and proactively mitigate risk with a comprehensive look at the latest consumer credit data. Download the June 2026 National Consumer Credit Trends Report now for essential market intelligence. Consumer Credit Observations: As of May 2026, total U.S. consumer debt was $18.23 trillion dollars, up 2.4% from May 2025. Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.52 trillion, making up 74.2% of total U.S. consumer debt. First mortgages were 95.0% of mortgage debt outstanding. Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOCs) were 3.3% of mortgage debt outstanding. Non-mortgage debt totaled $4.7 trillion in May 2026 and broke down into: 36.4% from auto loans and leases, 27.5% from student loans, 24.4% from credit card balances and 11.7% from other products. Auto Loans and Leases Observations: Total outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 2.4% from May 2025 to $1.71 trillion. The number of outstanding accounts in May 2026 was 87.4 million, a 0.3% increase year-over-year. The severe balance delinquency (60+ days past due) rate in May 2026 was 1.37%, which is comparable to May of last year. Bankcard Portfolio Observations: Outstanding balances on bankcards increased 3.7% from May 2025 to $1.1 trillion. The number of outstanding accounts was 594.4 million in May 2026, a 2.5% increase from May 2025. The severe balance delinquency rate (60+ days past due) as of May 2026 was 2.8%, which is a .01% decrease from May 2025 (2.81%). Average bankcard utilization for April 2026 was 20.3%, compared to 20.7% in May of 2025.
